what: The celibate, homeless life of renunciation as a recognized order of life (āśrama)

evidence.detail: Baudhāyana ascribes the division of the orders to the asura Kapila, son of Prahlāda, in rivalry with the gods — i.e. as foreign to the Veda.
The Taittirīya Āraṇyaka already calls the wind-girdled Vedic seers 'śramaṇas'.
Some scholars argue that the celibate orders entered Brahmanical dharma from the śramaṇa milieu; others see an internal Vedic development.

what: Rules of interpretation (nyāya) used to reconcile conflicting smṛti texts

evidence.detail: Medhātithi, Vijñāneśvara, Jīmūtavāhana and the digests cite Mīmāṃsā maxims by name.

what: The sequence breath-control, fixation, withdrawal, meditation; yogic powers

evidence.detail: MDh 6.72 names prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, pratyāhāra and dhyāna; YS 3.202–203 lists yogic powers; the relative dates of Manu and the Yoga Sūtra are uncertain, so direction is not asserted.

what: The figure of Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa and the name of a five-night (pañcarātra) sacrifice

evidence.detail: ŚB 13.6.1.1: Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa beholds the five-night sacrifice and becomes all.
A link to the later Pāñcarātra tradition's name has been proposed; not established.

what: Life-cycle sacraments, including an initiation with sacred thread, recast for Jain householders

evidence.detail: Jinasena's Ādipurāṇa gives Jain versions of the sacraments (kriyās) for householders.
